Controller-based CRUD and DTO validation

Find the route, input rules and response for each action inside the controller.

Open interactive lesson and complete code

What you are building

A student register organised with a controller

Build the same four student actions in a StudentsController file. A small input object checks the name and age before changes are accepted.

Student data is kept in memory and is lost when the app restarts.

Check the result

Create a valid student, then send an invalid age and compare the responses.

A controller puts related endpoints in one named class. It is like putting all student-counter instructions in one labelled folder.

How to test this example in Visual Studio

Download the project below, extract it into its own folder, then open StudyLab.csproj. Wait for NuGet restore. Choose Build → Build Solution. For console projects choose Start Without Debugging. For API projects use View → Terminal, make sure the terminal is in the folder containing StudyLab.csproj, then run the command shown in the lesson. Do not paste all files into Program.cs: use the exact file names displayed below.

Install and create the right project

  • Install Visual Studio with ASP.NET and web development and a .NET 10-compatible SDK. For WPF also install .NET desktop development. Check Tools → Get Tools and Features if templates are missing.
  • Create ASP.NET Core Empty for the Minimal API, or ASP.NET Core Web API with Use controllers for a controller project. Select .NET 10. Alternatively open the supplied .csproj to get exactly the lesson files.
  • Use a separate folder for every example. Delete the generated weather sample if it conflicts with the supplied files. Restore NuGet packages before building.
  • In View → Terminal, cd into the folder containing StudyLab.csproj. For local API testing run dotnet run --urls http://localhost:5100. Open requests.http and use Send Request above each request. Use the actual port from the console if you launch with a different profile.

Your first request

GET http://localhost:5100/api/students

Initially expect 200 OK with []. A browser address bar can send GET, but cannot conveniently send all CRUD methods. Use the .http editor, Postman, curl.exe or a Swagger UI. The JSON object is a data packet, not an HTML page.

Read the controller from top to bottom

  • [ApiController] turns model-validation failures into 400 responses. [Route("api/students")] is the shared URL prefix.
  • [HttpGet], [HttpPost], [HttpPut] and [HttpDelete] choose the HTTP verb. {id:int} accepts an integer route parameter.
  • Constructor injection supplies StudentStore from the container. Singleton means one store per application process; Scoped normally means one per HTTP request; Transient means a new instance when resolved.
  • StudentInput uses Required, StringLength and Range from System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations. A DTO limits what clients can set. Do not accept an entire database entity just because it is convenient.
  • CreatedAtAction uses the read-one action to build the Location URL. Action names are C# method names; route names and action names are not always the same thing.

Response shape and failure cases

POST /api/students
Content-Type: application/json

{"name":"Lefa","age":22}

Expected: 201 Created and {"id":1,"name":"Lefa","age":22} on a fresh store. Invalid JSON can fail before your action runs. A blank name or age outside 16-100 returns 400. An unknown ID returns 404. A successful PUT/DELETE returns 204; an empty response is correct.

Try it yourself

Why not let POST accept an Id chosen by the user?

Worked answer

The server should own identity assignment. A create DTO excludes Id and prevents accidental overwriting.

Add a course field safely.

Worked answer

Add Course to the model and input DTO, validate its length, map it in POST/PUT, then add request tests. A database-backed model also needs a migration.

Predict and practise

Should an age below the allowed range be accepted?

Check your prediction

No. The input rules reject it with a bad-request response.

Make one change

Find the DTO age rule. Send an invalid age and compare with a valid request.

Worked guidance

The DTO carries input. ApiController checks validation before running the action for invalid input.

Try independently

Create a new input validation rule and show one passing and one failing request.
